newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Asia to drive growth for Australia iron ore.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Asia to drive growth for Australia iron ore.

text.p: Australian iron ore exports are projected to increase by 12 percent to 152 million tonnes between 1996/97 and 2001/02, Peter Gooday, principal research officer at ABARE, said.
Gooday told the ABARE (Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics) Outlook in Canberra that Asian steel consumption would ensure growth in world steel markets.
Australia's iron ore exports were forecast to increase to 136 million tonnes in 1996/97 ending June 30, up strongly from 126.2 million tonnes the year before.
The value of exports was forecast to increase to A$3.1 billion in 1996/97 from A$2.9 billion in 1995/96.
Exports are projected to increase further, to 139 million tonnes in 1997/98, worth A$3.2 billion, ABARE material presented by Gooday showed.
East Asian producers were projected to increase their share of world steel production by 5.0 percent to 2001/02, he said.
The quantity and mix of exports of Australian steel-making raw materials would change with the ongoing development of new steel-making technologies, he said.

Sam Walsh, managing director of RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd unit Hamersley Iron's sales and marketing division, said Australia was well situated to supply steel- making raw materials to feed Asian steel production growth.
Value adding of iron ore was set to increase, Geremy Ingall, non-executive director of Kingstream Resources NL said.
Steel from the company's planned new mill near Geraldton, Western Australia, would be exported to Kingstream's joint venture partner, Taiwanese steel giant An Feng Steel Co Ltd, he said.
